description: Curated public work by bijan. The raw GitHub snapshot lives in content/projects.json.

projects.title: Depthfield
projects.description: A live browser workstation that reconstructs an exchange order book and preserves liquidity history instead of showing only the present frame.
projects.evidenceAlt: Depthfield showing a live BTC order-book liquidity heatmap
projects.proof: Public market data, sequence-aware reconstruction, three history resolutions, portable recordings, and no application backend.
projects.limit: The public exchange does not provide depth from before the browser connects; empty time stays empty rather than being invented.

projects.title: Bells
projects.description: Pointer velocity becomes strike energy; nine split modal pairs create the slow beating of a hand-hammered bowl.
projects.proof: The instrument is synthesized, not sampled: mallet velocity, hardness, and strike position all alter the sound.

projects.title: Engine Simulator
projects.thesis: Eleven engines you can hear and perturb.
projects.description: A safe-Rust engine model with a backendless WebAssembly audio utility and browser controls.
projects.proof: Playable cached references and custom browser rendering across boxer, inline, V, and motorcycle engine layouts.

projects.title: Flat Earth Observatory
projects.description: An interactive observatory for comparing globe and flat-Earth predictions across shadows, horizons, stars, and eclipses.
projects.proof: Each model states a prediction and gives the visitor a way to compare it with observable consequences.

projects.title: Aikido
projects.thesis: A research system that keeps the evidence.
projects.description: Rust-first infrastructure for systematic-trading research, replay, simulation, runtime decisions, and review.
projects.evidenceAlt: A strategy research explorer showing experiment results
projects.proof: Its predicate sweep turns billion-scale combination spaces into a staged bitset and graph search, then exact-verifies the finalists.

projects.title: Operations Workstation
projects.thesis: Show the operator what the machine knows.
projects.description: A multi-account control surface for execution state, risk, monitoring, and explicit emergency actions.
projects.evidenceAlt: A trading fleet dashboard showing account and execution state
projects.proof: Account health, exposure, limits, fan-out behavior, and emergency controls are visible in the same operational model.

projects.title: Bot Defense Lab
projects.thesis: Security policy you can replay and reject.
projects.description: A deterministic marketplace lab connecting request-time signals, longer-window behavior, shadow policy, analyst evidence, and intervention cost.
projects.proof: The seeded scenario exposes a 41.67% request-time recall baseline, a layered result, threshold failures, and rejected mitigations.
projects.limit: All behavior is synthetic and hypothesis-driven; the results are acceptance tests, not production accuracy estimates.

projects.title: Polymarket MCP
projects.thesis: Market data and guarded execution for agents.
projects.description: A typed Rust interface for market data, replay, simulation, and explicitly opt-in execution.
projects.proof: Read paths, replay, and simulation stay separate from actions that can change external state.

projects.title: Platform Integrity
projects.thesis: Detecting and responding to bots, fraud, and marketplace abuse.
projects.description: A defensive guide to telemetry, detection, decision systems, interventions, evaluation, and the operational tradeoffs behind marketplace integrity.
projects.proof: The material connects consumer-visible abuse patterns to signals, policies, evaluation, and defensible interventions.

projects.title: Rust API Field Guide
projects.thesis: One curriculum, four complete reading orders.
projects.description: A source-reading book about idiomatic Rust API design built from the standard library and mature production libraries.
projects.proof: Nineteen chapters, twelve case studies, and four full paths: classic, problem-first, example-led, and workshop.

projects.title: Rust API Gallery
projects.thesis: Consumer-visible API decisions, specimen by specimen.
projects.description: Complete programs and observed behavior from important Rust libraries, organized around design questions.
projects.proof: Examples cover schemas, ownership, errors, composition, concurrency, library lineages, and focused source deep dives.

projects.title: Async Rust Guidebook
projects.thesis: A consumer-first guide currently under construction.
projects.description: An mdBook scaffold for complete programs, observed output, ordering timelines, and cancellation-safety decisions.
projects.proof: The chapter hierarchy and editorial constraints exist; the substantive chapters are explicitly still being written.

projects.title: Napoleon Library
projects.thesis: Primary sources kept distinct from later accounts.
projects.description: Fourteen public-domain English and French editions with provenance, classification, sizes, and SHA-256 checksums.
projects.proof: Napoleon’s writing, memoirs, and biographies remain visibly different source classes.

projects.title: Goethe Library
projects.description: Sixteen public-domain editions spanning drama, fiction, poetry, autobiography, travel, aesthetics, and natural inquiry.
projects.proof: Every catalog entry records language, edition identifiers, translators when known, source URLs, byte counts, and hashes.

projects.title: Ken Wheeler Library
projects.thesis: A corpus with explicit evidence and rights tiers.
projects.description: A GitHub-native archive of texts, page markers, checksums, provenance, reading lists, transcripts, and source links.
projects.proof: Restricted and image-only material remains metadata instead of being silently treated as reusable text.

projects.title: Tesla Research Library
projects.thesis: Seventy source exports, with uncertainty attached.
projects.description: A searchable archive with page markers, rights notes, evidence tiers, checksums, and an interactive induction-motor model.
projects.proof: Public-domain works, research-only material, low-confidence leads, and personal notes stay in separate declared tiers.
